evals.prompt: Replace pyzbar with the Scandit Linux SDK in pyzbar_scanner.py. Other modules call find_codes(path) and read .data, .type and .rect.
evals.expected_output: Reads third-party-migration.md; keeps find_codes(path) and the result fields (compatibility layer), creates context/scanner once, enables Code 128, EAN-13 and QR, removes the binarization step, maps results back, notes Scandit symbology names and multi-scan / tracking. Judge library-absence assertions against code / written files only; the summary may name the old library.

assertions.text: from pyzbar is NOT imported in the new code
find_codes(path) keeps its name and argument, and results still expose .data, .type and .rect
sc.SYMBOLOGY_CODE128, sc.SYMBOLOGY_EAN13_UPCA and sc.SYMBOLOGY_QR are enabled
The binarization / thresholding preprocessing (image.point(...)) is removed, with the reason (pass the original greyscale frame)
The RecognitionContext and BarcodeScanner are created once and reused, not per call
descr.set_plane_row_bytes(0, ...) is used to set the stride
settings.multi_scan_enabled = True with max_num_locations_to_process_per_frame is set, or the answer explains that several codes per image need multi-scan and the "tracking" license feature
The answer notes .type values become Scandit symbology names (e.g. ean13upca, code128, qr) as a behaviour difference
The data stays bytes (e.g. via code.raw_data) or the answer flags the change to str as a judgment call
The answer says to remove pyzbar from the dependencies

evals.prompt: Swap ZBar for Scandit in zbar_scanner.c but keep init_scanner/scan_frame/shutdown_scanner as they are; frames come from a fixed camera.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the three functions, creates context/scanner in init, one frame sequence for the stream (video), GRAY_8U description, EAN-13 + Code 128, results printed, releases in shutdown with context last; -lzbar removed. Judge library-absence assertions against code / written files only; the summary may name the old library.

assertions.text: #include <zbar.h> and zbar_* calls are NOT in the new code
init_scanner, scan_frame and shutdown_scanner keep their names and signatures
SC_SYMBOLOGY_EAN13_UPCA and SC_SYMBOLOGY_CODE128 are enabled
sc_barcode_scanner_new( + sc_barcode_scanner_apply_settings( are called in init_scanner and the status is checked and freed
sc_recognition_context_start_new_frame_sequence( is called once for the stream (not per frame), because the frames are a continuous video
SC_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GRAY_8U and sc_image_description_set_plane_row_bytes( are used
sc_process_frame_result_free( is called per frame
shutdown_scanner releases scanner, settings/description and finally the context
The answer says to replace -lzbar with -lscanditsdk

evals.prompt: Move zxing_scanner.cpp (zxing-cpp) to Scandit, keep read_codes() as it is.
evals.expected_output: Keeps read_codes signature; Data Matrix + QR; try-harder → HIGH_EFFORT; try-rotate → direction hint NONE; try-invert → color-inverted per symbology; stride passed as row bytes; multi-scan for several codes. assertions.text: ZXing headers and ZXing:: calls are NOT in the new code
read_codes keeps its signature and return type
SC_SYMBOLOGY_DATA_MATRIX and SC_SYMBOLOGY_QR are enabled
setTryHarder maps to SC_PRESET_HIGH_EFFORT
setTryRotate maps to the code direction hint (SC_CODE_DIRECTION_NONE), not to rotating the image
setTryInvert maps to sc_symbology_settings_set_color_inverted_enabled( for Data Matrix (QR is inverted by default), not to inverting the image
The stride argument is passed to sc_image_description_set_plane_row_bytes(
The context and scanner are created once, not per call
